instruction.text: To see what Maya jewellery looked like, drag the earrings to the wealthy Maya man.

feedback.finish: The Maya wore big, heavy earrings. They would often stretch their earlobes as they believed that spirits could enter their bodies through the holes.

instruction.text: Now give him a nose piercing.
Finally, let’s give him a lip ring.

feedback.finish: Jewellery was very important to both the rich and poor Maya. Most people wore earrings, lip rings and necklaces, but nose rings were reserved for wealthy men.

atoms.b: The Maya wanted to look like their ((++gods animals)), some of which were portrayed with a pointed, flattened ((++head toe)). To copy this, the Maya pressed their ((++babies’ pets’)) heads between two wooden boards!
They would also file their ((++teeth hair)) into sharp points and hang small trinkets in front of their children’s faces to give them permanently ((++crossed blue)) eyes!
The Maya also gave themselves tattoos by ((++painting imagining)) a design onto their skin and then cutting along the lines. This would eventually scar over and form a colourful ((++tattoo poem)).
